Stan Vickers was first home in 14m. 47.6 secs. with Eric Hall 2nd and Dave McMullen 3rd, followed by three more of our walkers and scoring 14 a side, we won the match by 144 points to 262. Our handicap was won by ever improving Ray Switzer off 3 minutes and the Surrey W.C. handicap was won by A.

Other positions were Ted Smith 10th, Ray Switzer 18th, Harry Shields 21st Bob Readman 22nd, D. Russell 27th, Nick Milsum 28th, Wally Emery 29th and veteran Bert East 34th, totalling 11 of the 39 finishers.

Our return match with Surrey Walking Club at Tooting Bec was held on 14th August when a field of 41 turned out. We provided the first five men home with Eric Hall, Dave McMullen, Ted Smith, Ray Switzer and G.
Eric Hall gave up an individual place to push Ray Switzer along and finished 4th with Ray 5th and we easily won the team race with 10 points to Highgates 28 and Met.

The last track handicap of the season was held at Battersea Park on 20th August when a field of 17 turned out and was won by our most improved walker over the past few months, Ray Switzer off 300 yards in 14m. 8.6s.
Ray Hall gained revenge on Ray Switzer, Norman Guilmant smiled his way through and was last seen selling old football jerseys to the timekeepers.
Ray Switzer, ably backed up by Ray Hall, Dave Stevens and Eric Froude gained his 7 mile badge in this section. Peak of this meeting, is the "A" section, and we saw a grand performance by our lads.

Our three, Ray Middleton, Nick Milsum and Ray Switzer pursued a steady course together for the first half of the race and then began their advance through the field, with Middleton proving himself our best man on the day, finishing in 14th position.
To Ray Switzer a special word of praise on his first 'National' and also C. Edwards, who promises to develop into a first class distance walker.
Splendid backing up by Bob Newson, Ray Switzer and George Beecham ensured us of a clear team victory over Leicester W.C. by a margin of 12 pts.
We started a full team of eight, with Ray Switzer and Norman Guilmant as individuals. Our hopes rested on Eric Hall, second last year at Enfield where it rained throughout.
